key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cells lose energy and translate those losses into design rules for better device architectures.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers quantify bottlenecks in real PEC devices and prioritize fixes such as improved junction matching, co-catalysts, or nanostructuring.
method: Unifies BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes in one physically consistent loss model.
Generates I–V curves, efficiency maps, and ideal vs real-condition performance limits.
Fits experimental I–V data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract says the model was validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of experimental I–V fitting and parameter assumptions, so oversimplified inputs could misattribute loss pathways.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
